surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the sequential exposure of the surface to Ni(amd)2 and H2S pulses, leading to the formation of NiSx. The growth is self-limiting and occurs through surface reactions where Ni(amd)2 reacts with surface hydroxyl groups, followed by a water pulse to regenerate OH sites. The reaction is monitored in situ using QCM, showing a linear growth behavior with a growth rate of 9.3 ng/cm2 per cycle.
